summary: On a member that trims locally, closed agent and daemon mail in the graph now retires a week after it closes: all of a thread's message.* claims are deleted, their IDs join the retired set, and the freed pages go back to the filesystem. Person threads and any thread another claim cites are kept forever. This replaces the 2026-10-30 decision C15 (keep all messages forever) for non-person mail. MEASURED

replay.detail: A retired thread's claims leave this member's graph and their IDs enter retired_claim_ids in the deleting transaction, through the trim's own delete path (replica record, operation, event, signature and verdict rows, and every projection's delete trigger). The rule reads only claims, so every trim-local member retires the same threads with no coordination; peers compare the retained and retired sets, and admission refuses a retired ID, so none comes back.

schema.detail: No table, index or trigger change. Two meta keys: mail_retirement_closed_through (how far closed threads have been judged) and mail_retirement_deferred (a JSON list, at most 1,024, of threads judged before their sent claim arrived, judged again by later steps).

rules.detail: Retention of graph mail on trim-local members: message.* claims of a closed thread whose sender and recipient are not persons and that no other claim cites retire seven days after its message.closed was accepted. Members that do not trim locally, and [trim] mail = false, keep everything as before. Mail in the messages shard is not touched.

compatibility.detail: Mixed versions: an older member keeps its copies and never retires; it already holds what a retiring member no longer serves, and the retiring member's admission refuses those IDs, so replication stays whole (fleet::previous_release_beside_a_member_that_retires_closed_mail_and_its_rollback). Do not set [trim] mail in a config a previous release may read: its config parser refuses the unknown key; the default (on) needs no key.

downtime.detail: No migration. The daemon retires in its own task, starting 10-15 minutes after start, one writer hold of at most 40 ms at a time with a rest of four times the hold, and gives free pages back 128 at a time. HOLDS

manual.detail: No operator steps. [trim] mail = false keeps closed graph mail on a member that trims locally.

recovery.detail: Rolling back to the previous release keeps working: it reads the smaller store, its retired ledger is the same authority and refuses the retired IDs (verified by the fleet test above). Retired mail does not come back on a rollback; a member that must keep it sets [trim] mail = false before upgrading. Retirement steps and free-page steps commit at synchronous=NORMAL with no checkpoint inside the commit; the pragmas are put back around exactly those commits, on error too, so every other write keeps the member's own level. A crash or power loss can lose only the last retirement steps since the writer's previous ordinary commit; their claims are still there and the next pass retires them again.
